items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Gilmore had — took a gig with Art Blakey you know.

ctx.x: I may have a misconception about the group and how they operated, but is there enough to see how did those members of that group actually make a living? Were they making enough money to pay rent and eat?

At that time, see Sun Ra, he got there in ’58. I got there in 1960. He brought all his members from Chicago, mainly Ronnie Boykins, the bass player; Pat Patrick was the baritone saxophone player; Marshall Allen, alto; John Gilmore, tenor; and was using Clifford Jarvis on the drums and Lex Humphries. He had another drummer, it might have been Phil Grant, I’m not sure, from Chicago. But I worked with him with Lex Humphries you know. And no, all these guys, they were great musicians so that enabled them to work…

the New York scene as well as with Sun Ra. And Sun Ra would say, “Well I’m not going to pay — there’s not going to be that much money but you will become famous if you work with me.” I said, “Really?” Well he could talk. I mean he was a salesman, constantly selling. I mean he was really, his ideology, he was very astute, very articulate when it came to expressing ideas and whatnot. You know, and telling stories. Sometimes the rehearsal would go on just listening to his stories, to give you a concept.

items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Actually John Gilmore had went with Trane — I mean Art Blakey. He went with Art Blakey.

ctx.x: Oh when I first moved to New York I started working with Grant Green. Guitarist for Blue Note Records, he played bebop guitar. And he had Bob Cranshaw, Bob

Cunningham and Ben Dixon on drums and on tour instead he got an organ. Then sometimes we would play gigs with an organ. And then I got gigs with Hank Crawford. Now this was ’63. But meanwhile I would take little gigs with Sun Ra, with John Gilmore playing saxophone. Actually John Gilmore had went with Trane — I mean Art Blakey. He went with Art Blakey. And Sun Ra was using Pharoah but Trane was calling him all the time. John Coltrane was calling him all the time. So there I was, about the same age. So they tried…
May I ask if that’s the first time, first significant time that the idea of emotion and expression was introduced to you and came out of your horn?
